title: You May be Able to Get 43 More Minutes of Work Done if You Change Your Desk - Nautilus
gist: A Texas A&M study of 10,000+ workers at a large California energy company, tracking keystrokes and mouse activity, found sit-stand desks yield about 43 extra minutes of productivity per day.

insights.claim: A study in Theoretical and Applied Ergonomics found workers gained about 43 minutes of extra productivity per day by using a sit-stand desk.
insights.so_what: Supports corporate spending on adjustable office furniture and ergonomic products.
insights.quote: workers can squeeze 43 minutes of extra productivity out of their day, just by using a sit-stand desk
insights.speaker: Jake Currie

insights.claim: Texas A&M University researchers studied more than 10,000 workers at a large California energy company, combining comfort surveys with digital tracking of keystrokes, mouse clicks, words typed and typos.
insights.so_what: Shows how workplace digital surveillance data is being used to quantify productivity.
insights.locator: A team of occupational and public
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
